questions.scenario: You implement a change feed processor in .NET that generates embeddings for new and updated products. The processor runs on three App Service instances.
questions.question: Which component stores the processing progress for each partition key range and coordinates the work between the instances?

options.text: The monitored container
options.why: The monitored container holds the data whose changes are read. It does not store processor state.

options.text: The delegate
options.why: The delegate is the code that handles each batch of changes. It does not store progress.

options.text: The lease container
options.why: Correct. The lease container stores a lease per partition key range, which records the checkpoint and the owning instance.

options.text: The analytical store
options.why: The analytical store is a column store for analytics and is not used by the change feed processor.

questions.explanation: Leases in the lease container hold the checkpoint and ownership of each range, which lets instances share the work and resume after a failure.

questions.question: A change feed processor uses the default latest version mode. Items that are deleted from the monitored container must also be removed from a downstream search index. What should you do?

options.text: Set a soft-delete flag on items instead of deleting them, set a time to live (TTL) on the items, and handle the flag in the delegate
options.why: Correct. The flag change is recorded as an update in latest version mode, and TTL removes the item later.

options.text: Change the default consistency level to Strong
options.why: Consistency levels do not change which operations the change feed records.

options.text: Set the start time of the processor to the beginning of the container
options.why: Reading from the beginning does not add deletes, because latest version mode does not record them.

options.text: Add a second lease container
options.why: Lease containers store progress and do not change which operations are captured.

questions.explanation: Latest version mode does not capture deletes. Use a soft delete with TTL, or use all versions and deletes mode.

questions.question: You plan to scale a change feed processor across four compute instances so that the instances share the work. Which TWO configuration requirements must be met?

options.text: All instances use the same processor name and the same lease container configuration
options.why: Correct. Instances with the same processor name and lease container form one deployment unit that shares leases.

options.text: Each instance uses a different instance name
options.why: Correct. Each compute instance needs a unique instance name so that leases can be distributed between instances.

options.text: Each instance uses a different lease container
options.why: Separate lease containers create independent processors, and each one processes every change.

options.text: Each instance monitors a different container
options.why: To share the work on one container, all instances must monitor the same container.

questions.explanation: A deployment unit consists of instances with the same processor name and lease container but different instance names.

questions.question: A Python team must run code every time an item is inserted or updated in a Cosmos DB container. The team does not want to host or scale the processing infrastructure. What should you use?

options.text: An Azure Functions function with a Cosmos DB trigger and a lease container
options.why: Correct. The Cosmos DB trigger uses the change feed and manages leases and scaling for you, and it supports Python.

options.text: The change feed processor library in the azure-cosmos Python SDK
options.why: The change feed processor library is available in the .NET and Java SDKs, not in the Python SDK.

options.text: A timer-triggered function that queries the whole container every minute
options.why: Polling the whole container costs many RUs and does not reliably detect every change.

options.text: A stored procedure that runs after each write
options.why: Cosmos DB does not run stored procedures automatically after writes, and this would not hand changes to external code.

questions.explanation: The Azure Functions Cosmos DB trigger reads the change feed and stores leases, so the team writes only the handler code.

questions.question: A function triggered by the Cosmos DB change feed generates an embedding and writes it back into the same item. The function now runs continuously, even when no user changes data. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The lease container was created with the wrong throughput
options.why: Lease throughput affects speed and throttling, not whether changes repeat.

options.text: Writing the embedding back is an update that appears in the change feed and triggers the function again
options.why: Correct. The function must skip items whose source text has not changed, for example by comparing a stored hash, or write vectors to another container.

options.text: The change feed is in all versions and deletes mode
options.why: The mode does not cause a loop. Any mode records the function's own updates.

options.text: The account uses Session consistency
options.why: Consistency level does not cause the function to trigger again.

questions.explanation: Updates made by the handler to the monitored container are also changes. Add a guard, such as a content hash, to avoid an endless loop.
